title: Read CI proof for the selected comparison

intentCoverage.report:
**Caught.** For SEED-420#read-proof-for-the-comparison at `c972631bd688da776642a969e92e245fbf72024e`, the maintained mounted Chromium test rejected file Proof when it showed the default comparison during a captured landed run.

**Promise and fault.** Changes, Summary, and file Proof share the selected Baseline and Selection builds. In a detached scratch checkout, I removed the selected comparison from the evidence passed by `FileProofContent` in `dashboard/src/IntentFileProof.tsx`. The fixture and assertions stayed intact. The fixture distinguishes 1 → 9 selected cases from 4 default cases. [Scratch fault](/tmp/dough-intent-coverage-seed420-report.UKL1l6/fault.diff)

**Observation.** The maintained frontend command selected one case in `intent-story-compare-selected-counts.spec.ts`, “Changes, Summary and file Proof share the captured attempts and restore the default count.” Baseline passed. With the fault, the trace showed Changes and Summary still using 1 → 9. The screenshot independently showed Landed runs selected and the file Proof pane headed **Baseline compared with Landed**. The test caught the wrong pane at line 163 when `expectComparedProof` could no longer find its **Selection** column. The command selected one case after I removed an initial start anchor that matched zero tests against the runner’s prefixed titles. [Baseline proof](/tmp/dough-intent-coverage-seed420-report.UKL1l6/baseline-proof.json) · [Faulted trace](/tmp/dough-intent-coverage-seed420-report.UKL1l6/faulted.log) · [Faulted screenshot](/tmp/dough-intent-coverage-seed420-report.UKL1l6/faulted-file-proof.png)

**Restoration.** I restored the original file byte for byte, verified that the scratch Git status matched its initial clean state before and after the same focused test passed, and removed the scratch checkout. [Restored proof](/tmp/dough-intent-coverage-seed420-report.UKL1l6/restored-proof.json)

**Next proof action.** Keep the existing file Proof assertion for this fault.
